subject.title: Feature: Session labels / nicknames for easier identification

question: Should OpenClaw keep `label` as the canonical writable session name, migrate to canonical `title` with a compatibility mirror, or split the issue so CLI display is handled separately from Control UI `/new <name>` semantics?
rationale: Current main already has usable label APIs and `/name`, but the remaining open work changes user-facing command grammar and durable session metadata semantics, which require maintainer product/API intent before a safe implementation path.

options.title: Keep `label` canonical
options.body: Finish CLI and Control UI naming around the existing `label` field and reject new writable naming fields unless a separate migration is approved.

options.title: Adopt `title` canonicalization
options.body: Let the canonical-title PR define the durable field, migration, and compatibility behavior before closing the broader session-label issue.

options.title: Split remaining work
options.body: Track CLI label/listing polish separately while the Control UI `/new <name>` and title migration PRs proceed through maintainer review.

recommendation.title: Keep `label` canonical
recommendation.body: Finish CLI and Control UI naming around the existing `label` field and reject new writable naming fields unless a separate migration is approved.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the current label helper/resolve shape and recently changed the adjacent Control UI session grouping surface, making him the best available product/API routing owner from history.
